findings.actual_failure: Thirteen of the seventeen moved invocations — every shard-2 and shard-3 branch, including the shared-test dedup guard whose PR-red history is the recorded reason it is PR-gated — silently stop executing on every pull request. This is the exact consequence class AC-0007's cross-pin exists to prevent ('a shrunken matrix silently un-runs a branch's suites') and defeats AC-0001's invariant that every invocation runs in exactly one shard branch, reached through a dimension neither control reads. AGENTS.md's Always-do contract is that the equality pins 'redden on every workflow change, by design'; this one does not.
findings.observation: The dispatch step's `env: SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}` binding is the sole channel routing each matrix shard to its case branch, and its value is pinned by neither standing control. The posture test pins the dispatch run body verbatim (PINNED_DISPATCH_BODY, tools/test-build-check-workflow.py:505) and pins step-env KEY names only (_ALLOWED_STEP_ENV, tools/test-build-check-workflow.py:393-403, admits any SHARD value); lint-ci-parity's suite arm corroborates PR_GATED entries by step name and invocation paths (tools/lint-ci-parity.py:2952-2994) and never reads the env mapping. Verified empirically against scratch copies: mutating the workflow to `SHARD: shard-1` leaves `tools/test-build-check-workflow.py` audit() at zero violations and `tools/lint-ci-parity.py --root` exits 0; the sibling-matrix↔case cross-pin also stays satisfied because the case branches remain present and the matrix is unchanged.
findings.reachable_path: A future edit to .github/workflows/build-check.yml replaces the SHARD value with a constant or a PR-conditional expression (e.g. `SHARD: shard-1`, or `${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && 'shard-1' || matrix.shard }}`); every matrix shard then executes only shard-1's four invocations, each shard exits green, `needs.gate-catalogue-tests.result` is `success`, and the required aggregator `make build-check` passes — no red check anywhere.

findings.actual_failure: A maintainer reading the ledger to decide whether the duplicate-key class is held, and by which check, is told seven shapes were verified where six are enumerated, and that every recorded shape reddens the strategy pin — false for the duplicate `strategy:` spelling the mutation matrix carries. The repair must close the syntax class as claimed — separator-agnostic matching (any whitespace after ':' or '-'), name-charset-agnostic anchor/alias detection (digit-initial names), and merge-key detection that sees sequence and flow positions, or an equivalent whole-class rejection — and carry mutations proving the non-canonical spellings, so the ledger's 'anywhere in the workflow' claim is true.
findings.observation: The check's three regexes (tools/test-build-check-workflow.py:1544-1548) match only: merge keys whose '<<:' token sits at line start; alias/anchor tokens preceded by exactly one space after a colon or dash; anchor/alias names whose first character is a letter or underscore. Valid YAML spellings outside all three constraints escape the check: (a) two spaces after the colon before an anchor or alias ('x-defaults:  &d', '<<:  *d'); (b) a merge key in sequence position ('- <<: ...'), which is not at line start; (c) digit-initial anchor names ('&1d' / '*1d'). Verified by running the shipped audit() function on the shipped workflow mutated with these spellings: zero violations returned, while PyYAML 6.0.3 (the parser tools/lint-ci-parity.py:2868 uses to model the workflow) safe_load resolves the merge and lands the payload on the pinned steps. The four T9 mutations (tools/test-build-check-workflow.py:3051-3075) model only the canonical single-space, line-start, letter-initial spellings, so the self-test's 231-caught result proves nothing about these forms — the same proof-scope gap the ledger itself recorded for the T7 matrix check (QE-R4-002).
